events.title: The Umayyad army abandons its siege of Constantinople
events.description: The Umayyad army under Maslama ibn Abd al-Malik withdrew from Constantinople with heavy losses after a year-long siege by land and sea. Emperor Leo III's defenders had been helped by Greek fire, a harsh winter and Bulgar attacks.
events.html: The Umayyad army under Maslama ibn Abd al-Malik withdrew from Constantinople with heavy losses after a year-long siege by land and sea. Emperor Leo III's defenders had been helped by Greek fire, a harsh winter and Bulgar attacks.

events.title: Basques destroy Charlemagne's rearguard at Roncevaux
events.description: Basque fighters ambushed Charlemagne's rearguard in the Pyrenees, killing the commander Roland. The Song of Roland later recast the skirmish as a heroic stand against Saracens.
events.html: Basque fighters ambushed Charlemagne's rearguard in the Pyrenees, killing the commander Roland. The Song of Roland later recast the skirmish as a heroic stand against Saracens.

events.title: Macbeth is killed at the Battle of Lumphanan
events.description: King Macbeth of Scotland was killed at Lumphanan in Aberdeenshire by forces of Malcolm Canmore, Duncan's son. He had ruled for 17 years and even made a pilgrimage to Rome.
events.html: King Macbeth of Scotland was killed at Lumphanan in Aberdeenshire by forces of Malcolm Canmore, Duncan's son. He had ruled for 17 years and even made a pilgrimage to Rome.

events.title: The Cathar stronghold of Carcassonne falls to the crusaders
events.description: After a siege that began on 1 August, the fortified town of Carcassonne in Languedoc surrendered to the crusaders led by Arnaud Amaury. Under the negotiated surrender its inhabitants were allowed to leave free of harm.
events.html: After a siege that began on 1 August, the fortified town of Carcassonne in Languedoc surrendered to the crusaders led by Arnaud Amaury. Under the negotiated surrender its inhabitants were allowed to leave free of harm.

events.title: The Livonian Brothers of the Sword capture Tartu
events.description: The Livonian Brothers of the Sword, an order of German crusading knights, took Tartu, or Dorpat, the last major centre of Estonian resistance on the mainland. It became the seat of the Bishopric of Dorpat.
events.html: The Livonian Brothers of the Sword, an order of German crusading knights, took Tartu, or Dorpat, the last major centre of Estonian resistance on the mainland. It became the seat of the Bishopric of Dorpat.

events.title: Ignatius of Loyola and companions take vows at Montmartre
events.description: Ignatius and six companions vowed poverty and chastity in a chapel on Montmartre in Paris. The group became the Society of Jesus, approved by the Pope in 1540.
events.html: Ignatius and six companions vowed poverty and chastity in a chapel on Montmartre in Paris. The group became the Society of Jesus, approved by the Pope in 1540.

events.title: Napoleon Bonaparte is born in Corsica
events.description: Napoleone Buonaparte was born in Ajaccio, a year after France acquired Corsica from Genoa. He rose to become Emperor of the French and redrew the map and laws of Europe.
events.html: Napoleone Buonaparte was born in Ajaccio, a year after France acquired Corsica from Genoa. He rose to become Emperor of the French and redrew the map and laws of Europe.

events.title: Emperor Hirohito broadcasts Japan's surrender
events.description: For the first time, ordinary Japanese heard their emperor's voice as he announced acceptance of the Allied terms. The day is marked as VJ Day in Britain; the formal surrender was signed on 2 September.
events.html: For the first time, ordinary Japanese heard their emperor's voice as he announced acceptance of the Allied terms. The day is marked as VJ Day in Britain; the formal surrender was signed on 2 September.

events.title: India becomes independent as British rule ends
events.description: At midnight India became independent, a day after Pakistan. Partition uprooted perhaps 15 million people and communal violence killed hundreds of thousands, possibly up to two million.
